holidays.name: National Cherries Jubilee Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the flaming dessert of cherries doused in liqueur, set ablaze, and spooned over vanilla ice cream. Dinner and a show, all in one bowl!
holidays.origin: Cherries jubilee is credited to the famed French chef Auguste Escoffier, who created it for Queen Victoria's Golden or Diamond Jubilee celebration in the late 1800s. The exact origin of the national day is unclear, as with many food holidays.
holidays.funFact: The dessert is traditionally flambéed, meaning the alcohol is lit on fire at the table, which makes it one of the few desserts that can technically be called a controlled fire hazard.

holidays.name: National Punctuation Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the proper use of commas, semicolons, apostrophes, and all their pesky friends. Grammar nerds rejoice, and everyone else can double-check their texts.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2004 by Jeff Rubin, a newspaper editor and writer who runs a publishing and consulting business and who wanted to celebrate and promote correct punctuation use.
holidays.funFact: Celebrations traditionally include a punctuation-themed contest, and one famous example of why it matters is the sentence 'Let's eat, Grandma' versus 'Let's eat Grandma.' Commas save lives!

holidays.name: World Rhino Day
holidays.description: A global day of awareness for all five species of rhinoceros, whose populations are threatened by poaching and habitat loss. People celebrate with events, art, and social media campaigns.
holidays.origin: Started in 2010 by the World Wildlife Fund South Africa, and it has since grown into an international observance with participation from conservation groups all over the world.
holidays.funFact: A group of rhinos is called a 'crash,' which is an excellent name for a group of animals that can weigh over two tons and run up to around 30 miles per hour.

holidays.name: National Cherries Jubilee Day's Neighbor: Hobbit Day Eve
holidays.description: The day before Bilbo and Frodo Baggins' shared birthday on September 22 is long past, but fans keep the Shire spirit going with second breakfasts, pipe-weed-free parties, and marathon movie nights through the week.
holidays.origin: Hobbit Day was established by the American Tolkien Society in 1978 to honor the shared birthday of Bilbo and Frodo Baggins, and fans often extend the festivities.
holidays.funFact: Tolkien fans argue endlessly over how many meals a hobbit eats per day, with the usual answer being seven, including breakfast, second breakfast, elevenses, luncheon, afternoon tea, dinner, and supper.

holidays.name: Festival of Sacred Rhyme: Native Plant Seed Collecting Season Kickoff (Unofficial)
holidays.description: Not an official holiday, but late September is a popular time for gardeners to begin collecting seeds for next year's blooms, turning backyards into tiny treasure hunts.
holidays.origin: Gardening communities and native plant societies encourage seed collecting at the turn of autumn when many wildflowers and grasses have gone to seed.
holidays.funFact: Some seeds, like those of milkweed, are designed to travel by fluffy parachute, and a single plant can release hundreds of silky-tufted seeds on the autumn wind.
